Convoluted story, but if you pay attention to details you will get it. Hands down best atmosphere in a VR game, and it's not even close. Controls are average, and the whole game has this janky feel to it that might put some off. Personally, I love the jank.

Excellent showcase of VR interactivity and physics at an extreme level, to a point where the physics can get janky (arms clipping into objects you're holding, etc.).

If you like HL: Alyx, and are curious how its gameplay/combat might be if the realism were taken up two notches, give Boneworks a try. You can sprint, jump manually, dynamically adjust your standing/crouching height, climb ledges, and all sorts of other movement features that HL: Alyx has simplified. Some of these mechanics take practice to nail down, but you'll be executing them with relative ease once you do.

As mentioned in the opening sentence, just be warned about the body physics not working perfectly. Also, the realism is right under the border of tedium/troublesome-ness, so it might not be for everyone.

EDIT: And new features being added continuously for free (including a few levels and game modes)! Very worth supporting this game.

Now usually I wouldn't write a review for any games I've played and if I did it would probably be a joke review, but this game has impressed me so much and keeps on making me play over and over I just had to say something about this game. It's good. the guns are realistic and fun to use, the style can go to a dark, creepy, damp sewers to a huge futuristic gigantic power room, the story while confusing at first slowly make more sense once you take a close look at it. I love the way this game takes traveling MythOS. But while their is a lot of very good points, there could be some improvements such as, more difficult NPCs, some new guns that aren't a pistol or automatic, workshop support could be nice, and I've had not that much problems whit it but I've heard people talk about problems with the physics. I love this game because of how much it can improve and how much it had improved. Keep up the good work Stress Level Zero!

While the technology behind the game can be fairly impressive at times, I honestly don’t think the tech alone is enough to carry an entire game. This is essentially a a glorified tech demo - one that has its moments, sure, but they’re too few and far between in an already very short experience.

A lot of the gameplay also feels frustrating to deal with, mostly due to how clunky and awkward certain mechanics and controls are. The story is about what you’d expect from a glorified tech demo...and that’s probably all that needs to be said about it.

The level design, art direction, and enemy design are all bland, uninspired, and honestly very unpleasant to look at, especially in VR, where everything is right in your face. The game in general is simply very ugly...and kind of nauseating to look at.

I guess, there is some mindless fun to be had after finishing the main story, when you can mess around with the physics and various items, but I really don’t see the thirty-dollar value here. At best, you might get an hour or two of light sandbox fun before getting bored.

Should you play it just to experience the tech behind it? Meh...probably not.

Definitely the must have VR game alongside Bonelabs. I strongly think that this kind of physically interactive environment is what makes VR immersive.

Janky and a bit buggy at times but overall it's a lot of fun and a good way to introduce yourself to VR.

Tutorial is fun and is effective at showing you how to play the game as well as introduce you to the game's story. Gunplay is fun. Moving around and looking at everything is fun. Melee is good. Story is... serviceable. It's kinda just there to push the game along, which is fine, and it doesn't interfere. 

Now maybe it's because it's VR in general, but picking up, moving objects, trying to break objects, and climbing, while fun, can be pretty jank at times. I did get frustrated at times especially trying to climb. The good news is often there are several ways to deal with different parts of the game typically, so you aren't pigeonholed to do things the hard way. 

A significant criticism is that near the end of the game there are just flat out NO save points after a certain point. And I'm wondering if I died, would I have to do ALL THAT WORK over again. Not sure but I'm glad I didn't find out. There might at least have been a checkpoint system at that point, but again, I'd rather not have found out. 

Otherwise yea, very much worth it for a VR game. I played it on a HTC Vive Pro 2 with Valve Index Controllers.

I bought this game back when I got my Oculus Quest 2, and boy do I love this game. The game is long, for a VR game, there's multiple add-on modes that expand your post game playtime and there's collectibles you could spend your time getting. I actually like the movement in this game more than Half-Life: Alyx.

This game is one of the only VR experiences where you actually physically exist in the world and that really, really makes a difference for immersion. The gunplay is some of the best and the story is very well done.

Environment Graphics are simplistic but nice, and performance is way better than most VR games on my 1070.

Puzzles and platforming can be EXTREMELY physically demanding and frustrating, I love that aspect of it but if you do not have full range of motion in your IRL joints you will have some issues completing the story.

Lastly there is a large number of mods available and a working modloader

What an amazing game. I've only finished the first level and this does feel like a mix of half-life/portal, with both shooting and amazing puzzles and similar styles. The physics are incredible, and the lack of holding back of tossing you around like a rag doll is a fresh of air for someone who is an experienced VR user.

My only negative comment is the inability to save your state and resume, forcing you to commit to a longer session than you might otherwise be able to provides since you have to complete a level or be forced to restart it next time you play. If you're new and prone to motion sickness, avoid this game, because if you leave once you're sick, you'll need to restart again.

Boneworks is a perfect example of everything that a VR game should have. Simulated weight, full bodies with physics, and interacting with the environment as one of the key mechanics in progressing through the game. you can pick up, push, pull, and throw just about everything you see. Half of those things are destructible. You can knock over those fancy looking vending machines with enough effort. To be honest, I spent way too much time flipping every table I saw in the game.
This is one of the best VR games out there right now.
Great gameplay, mediocre story at best. I don't know why it's still so expensive for a vr game even on sale. Mid and nothing more.

Some of the levels drag on a bit, I especially hate the cardboard boxes everywhere, despite some frustrating moments, I really enjoy the puzzles and the VR pistols and rifles in this game, the smgs are sort of shit though. The climbing is a bit wonky, once you get used to it it's really not a big deal though, you just have to figure it out. So far I have beaten the main story levels and unlocked a bunch of stuff by thoroughly searching the levels, played some sandbox modes, and some arena modes so a bit of everything. I especially enjoy the arenas. I still have a lot to unlock and extra modes to play after beating the story which is awesome. I'd definitely recommend this game to anyone looking for a puzzle shooter style sandbox game that doesn't bog you down with story. The acting in it was definitely pretty damn corny but it's okay haha, it doesn't happen much and it's not a big deal, you can tell the game really isn't about the story it's about the gameplay.

This game is the best VR game of all time.

The OST is oddly nostalgic, intense, and just great to listen to, the atmosphere is amazing (reminiscent of Portal), it's immersive as all hell, and the gameplay is so much fun with all the melee weapons being physics-based, and the guns being... well, guns. Can't really go wrong with VR guns (unless you make the reloads automatic).

There's almost too much content in this game, too. I've been playing for 57 hours so far and I doubt I've even gotten through half the game's content (granted, I did spend most of my time messing around with brutal takedowns and admiring the beautiful environments this game offers).

The only thing keeping me from spending hours upon hours each day playing this game is my Quest 2 having abysmal comfort and constantly applying pressure to my forehead, and the thumbsticks eventually hurting my thumbs after a while.

In short: If you have the money, a VR headset, and a strong enough PC, definitely consider this game along with Beat Saber and Half Life: Alyx.

This is the best VR shooter-puzzler I've tried so far, but I haven't tried Alyx yet. I have to say, the inventory system is absolutely perfect, no clunky mechanics such as INTO THE RADIUS's magazine and spaghetti backpack storage. Complicated inventory systems are best kept to mouse and keyboard, where one can meticulously sort their items without having to try to grab a bracelet that is stuck in fifteen different boxes in a suspended state.

The gun play isn't fully realistic (UZI, MP5 locking back, no bolt release on AR), but it's pretty good. Give it a try.
